_source: Transcribed from the Claude Design handoff bundle's DISTRICTS/GROUPS constants in Curia.dc.html (fetched 2026-07-30). lat/lon/base/r/span are the prototype's own map-projection values, kept as-is so the real map behaviour can be ported rather than re-derived.
_accentColorSource: The five Cheshire districts' original accentColor values (transcribed from the prototype, per CLAUDE.md's Design tokens table) all sat in a narrow gold/tan/olive hue range — technically distinct hex values, but not perceptually distinct once rendered as the real map's low-opacity blurred glow (2026-08 user report, testing from Wilmslow: 'the districts are all glowing the same colour'). Widened the hue spread for these five specifically (gold → amber → terracotta → rust-brown → olive) while staying inside the closed warm palette CLAUDE.md's Design tokens section governs — per that section's own note, per-district accent colors are explicitly 'extensible... not a fixed set', unlike the core UI palette. Manchester's five (2026-08, same user, same complaint against a Manchester screenshot this time, with explicit requested hues: 'northern quarter is a purple, deansgate is an orange, spinningfields a soft blue') now deliberately step outside the warm-only cluster — purple/blue read as genuine outliers against CLAUDE.md's 'avoid bright primary colors' general aesthetic note, so both are kept desaturated/dark-mode-muted (plum and slate, not violet and cyan) rather than literal primaries, and are only 2 of the 5 so the family still reads warm overall. Ancoats and Chinatown weren't named by the user; picked a rust-brick and a crimson-berry respectively to keep real hue separation from Deansgate's orange and from each other. The user's own scoping note applies here too: colors only need to be distinct from what's actually visible together — Northern Quarter's purple can freely be reused by a far-off district (e.g. Hale) without conflict, since the two are never both zoomed-in at once.
_editorialDescriptionSource: Added by curia-moments-journeys (M6) for the district guide screen. Northern Quarter/Ancoats/Spinningfields/Deansgate are transcribed (Ancoats lightly trimmed to drop a specific venue count tied to the prototype's own DETAIL.v list, which doesn't match this file's seed venues) from the prototype's own DETAIL constant. Chinatown/Altrincham/Hale/Wilmslow/Alderley Edge/Mobberley have no DETAIL entry in the prototype (it falls back to a generic Cheshire blurb for any district without one) — their copy below is original, written to the Brand voice bar in CLAUDE.md, not transcribed.
_metroScopeNote: Los Angeles (Beverly Hills, West Hollywood, Santa Monica, Venice, Culver City) was added as a real metro in an earlier 2026-08 pass, then removed at explicit later request (2026-08) to keep the app scoped to Manchester/Cheshire only. This coincidentally restores CLAUDE.md's own 'Districts — resolved to the prototype's real 10, across two metros' section to being accurate again — it was already stale while LA existed, and was flagged as such but never updated in CLAUDE.md itself while that was true.
_prestburyCheadleHulmeKnutsfordSource: Prestbury, Cheadle Hulme and Knutsford added 2026-09-03 at explicit user request ('prestbury, cheadle hulme, knutsford, to name a few' — the daily research pipeline had been finding venues within the existing 10 districts only, never proposing a genuinely new one, despite these being obvious real gaps). Coordinates verified via web search, not invented: Prestbury 53.288/-2.151 (the historic village core, 'The Village'/'The Stocks'), Cheadle Hulme 53.376/-2.190, Knutsford 53.3031/-2.3748 (the same figure already verified for The Commons by Curia's town data). All three pass the coordinate sanity check the review agent applies to venues (lat 53.0-53.6, lon -2.6--2.0). Cheadle Hulme is administratively in the Metropolitan Borough of Stockport, Greater Manchester, not Cheshire — assigned metro 'cheshire' anyway on real historic-county identity and character (leafy, suburban, not urban-Manchester), the same precedent Wilmslow Golf Club already set (seeded in Mobberley by real location, not by name). `base` scores are reasoned estimates (matching how the original ten were seeded pending real curation) — Prestbury and Cheadle Hulme sit near Mobberley's low end since neither has curated venues yet; Knutsford sits higher, reflecting genuine everyday commercial activity (an indoor market hall trading four days a week, a monthly makers' market) already documented for The Commons. accentColor values extend the existing gold/amber/terracotta/rust-brown/olive Cheshire spread with three more perceptually distinct warm tones: walnut-brown for Prestbury, khaki-olive for Cheadle Hulme, sandy amber for Knutsford. Populating each with real, independently-vetted venues is separate follow-up work, not done here — these are district entries only, same starting point Mobberley and Chinatown once had.
_goldenTriangleCorrectionNote: 'The Golden Triangle' district group below previously listed alderley-edge/wilmslow/mobberley/hale — but the real, named Cheshire term (verified 2026-09-03: Great British Life, Wikipedia's own 'Golden Triangle (Cheshire)' entry, multiple estate-agent sources) canonically means Alderley Edge, Prestbury and Wilmslow specifically, with Knutsford and Mobberley sometimes included in broader usage. Prestbury and Knutsford added to the group now that both exist as real districts; Mobberley and Hale were left in place rather than removed — broader-usage sources do support their inclusion, and this is additive correction (fixing a real gap), not a wholesale redefinition nobody asked for.
_chorltonSource: Chorlton added 2026-09-06 by curia-suggestion-review, promoted from docs/data/district-suggestions.json after independent re-verification. A genuine, distinct south Manchester district (Chorlton-cum-Hardy, ~3-5 miles SW of the city centre, bordering Stretford/Sale/Didsbury/Withington) that doesn't overlap any of the existing 5 Manchester districts, all of which are inner-city/central. Confirmed via creativetourist.com, manchestersfinest.com and confidentials.com as having an unusually independent, chain-resistant food/drink scene centred on Beech Road and Chorlton Green, plus a real, named craft-beer trail (the Chorlton Beer Mile, ~8 independent taprooms). Coordinates (53.4390/-2.2790) verified against Chorlton Library and other listed buildings in the immediate area, which cluster at 53.438-53.444/-2.278--2.283. accentColor is a muted sage/forest green (#6B8F71), distinct from every other Manchester district's purple/rust-brick/soft-blue/orange/crimson-berry accents — chosen to read as 'leafy village green' rather than a bright primary, per CLAUDE.md's general aesthetic note. Its first three real venues (The Edge Theatre & Arts Centre, The Chorlton Tap, Bar San Juan) were independently verified and promoted 2026-09-07 — see docs/data/venues.json's own note for that run.
_didsburySource: Didsbury added 2026-09-07 by curia-suggestion-review, promoted from docs/data/district-suggestions.json after independent re-verification. A genuine, distinct south Manchester suburb (Didsbury Village around School Lane plus West Didsbury along Burton Road, ~2.5km east of Chorlton across the Mersey, with its own separate identity) that doesn't overlap any of the existing 6 Manchester districts. Confirmed via confidentials.com, creativetourist.com and designmynight.com as a well-known, independent-heavy food and drink destination (Lime Tree — the city's longest-running suburban fine-dining room; Volta; FOLK on Burton Road), distinct in character from Chorlton's beer-mile/tapas-strip identity. Coordinates (53.4176/-2.2310) re-checked against the M20 6RD postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk) — School Lane, Didsbury Village. accentColor (#B98098, dusty rose) re-checked for perceptual distinctness against every other Manchester district accent (Northern Quarter's plum, Ancoats' rust-brick, Spinningfields' soft blue, Deansgate's orange, Chinatown's crimson-berry, Chorlton's sage green) — distinct. No venues seeded yet — same starting point Chorlton had before its own first venue pass 2026-09-07; populating it with real, individually-verified venues is separate follow-up work.
_stockportUnderbanksSource: Stockport (Underbanks) added 2026-09-08 by curia-suggestion-review, promoted from docs/data/district-suggestions.json after independent re-verification. A genuine, distinct, well-documented independent food-and-drink regeneration quarter (Stockport Council's own 'Rediscovering the Underbanks' funded regeneration, ~£7m including National Lottery Heritage Fund money; local coverage explicitly calls it 'Stockport's Northern Quarter') centred on the historic Market Place/Underbanks streets — a Victorian market hall, a cluster of independent bars in old bank vaults, and Where the Light Gets In, which holds a genuine Michelin Guide listing (a Michelin Green Star for sustainability plus 4 AA Rosettes, not a standard Michelin star — copy below doesn't overstate this). Coordinates (53.4112/-2.1564) re-checked and land almost exactly on the Market Place/SK1 1EW postcode centroid, squarely in the Underbanks itself, not elsewhere in Stockport and not overlapping the existing Cheadle Hulme district (a separate, leafy, suburban part of the same borough several miles south). Named 'Stockport (Underbanks)' rather than plain 'Stockport' since only this specific quarter is being added, not the whole town. Metro assigned 'manchester'/'city': Stockport is administratively its own Metropolitan Borough, not the City of Manchester, but it's one of Greater Manchester's ten boroughs and the Underbanks itself reads as dense urban regeneration (market hall, railway viaduct, bank-vault bars), closer in character to Chorlton/Ancoats/Northern Quarter than to any Cheshire county town — 'manchester' is used as Greater Manchester shorthand here, the same judgment call flagged by the original candidate and upheld on re-verification. accentColor (#7A3B3E, deep brick-wine) re-checked for perceptual distinctness against every existing accent, closest neighbours being Chinatown's crimson-berry (#A73F52) and Ancoats' rust-brick (#9C5030) — both notably brighter/more orange than this darker, more maroon tone. No venues seeded yet — same starting point Chorlton and Didsbury each had before their own first venue passes; populating it with real, individually-verified venues is separate follow-up work.
_heatonMoorSource: Heaton Moor added 2026-09-09 by curia-suggestion-review, promoted from docs/data/district-suggestions.json after independent re-verification. A genuine, distinct south Manchester/Stockport suburb (part of 'The Heatons') that doesn't overlap Stockport (Underbanks) (a several-hundred-metre-distant, wholly different regeneration/market-hall quarter) or Cheadle Hulme (several miles further south). Confirmed via hardens.com, squaremeal.co.uk and independent local coverage as having its own real, independent-heavy food and drink strip on Heaton Moor Road/Shaw Road, anchored by the Savoy Cinema — an independent 1923 picture house, closed 2014, reopened 2015 by the Mundin family, re-confirmed still trading via manchestersfinest.com/the cinema's own site. Coordinates (53.4213/-2.1857) re-checked against Heaton Moor Road and land within the existing sanity box. accentColor (#6B7F94, dusty slate blue) re-checked for perceptual distinctness against every existing Manchester-metro accent — no other district reads blue-grey. Metro assigned 'manchester'/kind 'city' on the same Greater-Manchester-shorthand judgment already applied to Stockport (Underbanks) and Cheadle Hulme. No venues seeded yet — same starting point Chorlton, Didsbury and Stockport (Underbanks) each had before their own first venue passes; populating it with real, individually-verified venues is separate follow-up work.
_macclesfieldSource: Macclesfield added 2026-09-11 by curia-suggestion-review, promoted from docs/data/district-suggestions.json after independent re-verification. A genuine, distinct Cheshire market town (its own royal charter from 1261, a real silk-manufacturing heritage — Silk Museum, Paradise Mill — and an independent food/drink scene documented via visitcheshire.com/visitmacclesfield.co.uk) that doesn't overlap Prestbury, which this file's own existing note already describes as a satellite village downstream of Macclesfield's silk money, roughly 3 miles away. Fresh re-verification (2026-09-11) confirmed Macclesfield's Market Hall reopened after a £2.4m refurbishment on 24 February 2026, and the monthly Treacle Market (running since 2010, one of the largest artisan markets in the North West) is still active with 2026 dates published — both current, positive signals for the town's real, ongoing commercial life, not stale coverage. Coordinates (53.2611/-2.1257, the Market Place/St Michael and All Angels centroid) re-checked and land within the sanity box. accentColor (#4F6B63, muted verdigris/mill-green) re-checked for perceptual distinctness against every existing accent — no other district reads this cool a green. Not added to 'The Golden Triangle' district group: the canonical definition already resolved in this file (see _goldenTriangleCorrectionNote) is specifically Alderley Edge/Prestbury/Wilmslow, sometimes Knutsford/Mobberley — Macclesfield is the market town those villages sit around, not itself a Golden Triangle village. No venues seeded yet — same starting point every prior district promotion has had before its own first venue pass.
_nantwichSource: Nantwich added 2026-09-12 by curia-suggestion-review, promoted from docs/data/district-suggestions.json after independent re-verification. A genuine, distinct Cheshire market town roughly 15 miles south of Knutsford — the southernmost existing Cheshire district — with no overlap with any other district in this file. Re-confirmed via nantwichtowncouncil.gov.uk, greatbritishlife.co.uk and visitcheshire.com: real Grade I/II-listed Tudor, Georgian and Victorian architecture, one of the country's finest medieval parish churches (St Mary's), a three-day-a-week traditional market, and an independent-heavy shopping and eating scene explicitly documented as such by the town's own council directory — the same 'a local would name it without hesitation' gap this file's review process exists to catch, alongside Knutsford/Prestbury/Wilmslow. Coordinates (53.067/-2.5206, St Mary's Church/town centre) land within the lat 53.0-53.6/lon -2.6--2.0 sanity box. accentColor (#A56A52, faded brick-clay) re-checked for perceptual distinctness against every existing accent, closest neighbours Alderley Edge (#A66B4F) and Wilmslow (#B85C3E) — distinct from both, and Nantwich is never zoomed alongside either given the real distance between them. Not added to any districtGroup — it sits well outside the Golden Triangle's real geography. No venues seeded yet — same starting point every prior district promotion has had before its own first venue pass.
_tarporleyNorthwichCorridorSource: Tarporley and Northwich added 2026-09-18 at explicit user request, to close a real visual gap: Chester and Nantwich (17.5 miles apart, the shortest link between either and the rest of the Manchester/Cheshire cluster) rendered as isolated islands on the map's coverage-territory shape, which unions each district's own 5.5-mile buffer (COVERAGE_RADIUS_MILES, src/lib/map/geo.ts) rather than reading the `metro` field — two circles need to sit within 11 miles of each other to visually connect. Rather than force a fake connection or remove Chester/Nantwich, researched whether a real, worthwhile town actually sits in the gap. It does, twice over: Tarporley (9.3mi from Chester, 8.9mi from Nantwich — both under the 11-mile threshold) and Northwich (9.6mi from Tarporley, 6.4mi from Knutsford, the nearest main-cluster district) together form a real chain — Chester-Tarporley-Nantwich on one side, Tarporley-Northwich-Knutsford on the other — that fully connects the whole cluster into one shape, entirely as a side effect of adding two districts that are genuinely worth adding on their own editorial merit, not built as bridge points. Tarporley: verified via chesterstandard.co.uk, letstalkbizcw.co.uk and the parish council's own site as a village whose high street has 'resisted the chain-store drift' almost entirely (independent butchers, a fishmonger, a bookshop, galleries) — a real, specific, sourced claim, not a generic 'quaint village' assumption. Coordinates (53.160043/-2.669352) from the High Street post office postcode (CW6 0DX, postcodes.io). Northwich: verified via visitnorthwich.co.uk as a real salt town (the same 'wich' = brine etymology Nantwich's own note already documents) on the River Weaver, rebuilding its high street via the Barons Quay redevelopment — honestly mixed with some national retailers per the same source, not a purely independent scene the way Tarporley's is, but a real and growing one. Coordinates (53.26211/-2.512439) from the town-centre postcode (CW9 5DH). accentColor: Tarporley a muted hedgerow-green (#5E6E4F), checked for distinctness against Chorlton's brighter sage (#6B8F71) and Macclesfield's verdigris (#4F6B63); Northwich a river-slate teal (#4A6B6E), checked against Heaton Moor's dusty blue-grey (#6B7F94) and Spinningfields' soft blue (#6E8FA6) — distinct from both. Both kind 'county'. base scores are reasoned estimates, same convention as every other first-pass district: Northwich (58) above Tarporley (48) — a proper town centre with an active redevelopment versus a smaller village high street. No district group added — neither fits an existing group's real geography (Golden Triangle is specifically Alderley Edge/Prestbury/Wilmslow/Knutsford/Mobberley), and a two-district 'the corridor' group felt like grouping for its own sake rather than a real, named local identity. Both seeded with 3 real, individually-verified first venues (see venues.json's own note) — enough to clear MIN_MATCHES_TO_RANK and actually appear in the redesigned Districts view, not the usual 'no venues yet' starting point, since the whole point of this addition was for these two to actually render.
_chesterSource: Chester added 2026-09-16 by curia-suggestion-review, promoted from docs/data/district-suggestions.json after independent re-verification. A genuine, nationally well-known Cheshire city — city status, a cathedral, the UK's most complete Roman/medieval walls, and the double-decker Rows — with no overlap with any existing district; the nearest, Nantwich, sits roughly 17 miles south with a wholly different small-market-town character. Independently re-confirmed via fresh search (Tripadvisor, chester.com, visit-chester.co.uk, walkingfoodtoursuk.co.uk): a real, current, independent-heavy food and drink scene distinct from anywhere else in this file (Shrub, Olive Tree Brasserie, Paysan, Craft & Company, Beer Heroes, Porta tapas near the Northgate, Huxley's) alongside the Rows/walls/cathedral as genuine Do-category draws — a different, and larger, set of names than the original candidate cited (Sticky Walnut, The Coach House, etc.), which reads as the scene having moved on since research rather than either list being wrong; both independently confirm the same underlying claim (a real, current, non-chain-dominated scene), so not treated as a discrepancy worth blocking on. Coordinates (53.1909/-2.8888, the Eastgate Clock) are a real, precise, independently verifiable landmark, not an estimate — flagged on re-verification for sitting just outside this file's usual lon -2.6 sanity-box edge (Chester is genuinely further west than every other seeded district), but judged not 'wildly outside' in the sense that check exists to catch (a research error putting a venue in the wrong country/region): Chester is Cheshire's own county city, its location is unambiguous and extremely well-documented, and the box was calibrated against the 20 districts seeded so far, not against Cheshire's actual westward extent. accentColor (#A6512F, sandstone-red) re-checked for perceptual distinctness — closest neighbours Ancoats' rust-brick (#9C5030, more orange/brown) and Nantwich's faded brick-clay (#A56A52, notably lighter/pinker) — distinct from both, and Chester is never zoomed alongside either given the real distance involved. No venues seeded yet — same starting point every prior district promotion has had before its own first venue pass.
_bramhallSource: Bramhall added 2026-09-10 by curia-suggestion-review, promoted from docs/data/district-suggestions.json after independent re-verification. A genuine, distinct Stockport village with real Cheshire-village character (I Love Bramhall, manchestersfinest.com and area-guide sources all describe its own centre and independent-heavy high street) anchored by Bramall Hall, a Grade I-listed Tudor manor, with its own Village Square/high street businesses (Plum Cake, Pix Pizza, Brooklyn Quarter and others per adamsimms.exp.uk.com/shrigley-rose.co.uk). Fresh re-verification found its real-world distance to Cheadle Hulme is closer to 2 miles (~3.2km) than the original candidate's 2.6km estimate — flagged as worth a second look, but judged not disqualifying: this file already has closer district pairs with distinct identities (Heaton Moor/Stockport Underbanks a few hundred metres apart, Didsbury/Chorlton ~2.5km apart), and Bramhall's high street and character read as genuinely separate from Cheadle Hulme's. Administratively part of the Metropolitan Borough of Stockport, not the historic county of Cheshire — assigned metro 'cheshire' anyway on the same real historic-county-identity/leafy-suburban-character judgment already made for Cheadle Hulme. accentColor (#7D6B87, muted heather-plum) re-checked for perceptual distinctness against every existing accent, closest neighbours Northern Quarter's plum (#8B6FA8) and Didsbury's dusty rose (#B98098) — distinct from both. No venues seeded yet — same starting point every prior district promotion has had before its own first venue pass.
_imerovigliCoordinateCorrectionSource: 2026-09, at explicit user report ('some venues are showing as in the ocean'): Imerovigli's centroid below (36.4278/25.4177) was a hand-picked guess made when this district was first added, never actually verified against a real geocode — a point-in-polygon check against Santorini's real landmass shape (see docs/data/venues.json's own _santoriniCoordinateCorrectionSource note for the full methodology) found it sitting in the caldera, ~600m from Imerovigli's real village centre, and it was the shared root cause of 5 of the 10 mis-placed venues that report surfaced. Corrected to 36.4325579/25.4228307 — Imerovigli's real village centroid, independently confirmed via Nominatim (osm_type node, place=village) and re-verified on-land by the same polygon check.
_santoriniSource: Santorini added 2026-09 at explicit user request — Curia's first destination outside Manchester/Cheshire, for a real member (a friend of the user's) travelling there right now who wants to test the app. Four real, distinct districts chosen to match the island's actual geography rather than one undifferentiated 'Santorini' blob: Oia (the clifftop sunset village, luxury boutiques and fine dining), Fira (the actual capital — caldera-view restaurants by day, the island's real nightlife strip after dark), Imerovigli (the quiet, highest-point caldera village between Oia and Fira, serious hotel terraces), and Perissa & Perivolos (the black-sand beach coast on the southeast side, where the island's beach clubs actually are — a good 8km from the caldera villages and a genuinely different kind of day). Coordinates are each area's real, well-known centre point (Oia's castle/sunset-viewing area, Fira's main square, Imerovigli's caldera path, the Perissa-Perivolos beach road roughly midway between the two). accentColor values step outside the existing warm Manchester/Cheshire palette into Aegean-appropriate tones (caldera blue for Oia, sunset terracotta for Fira, a cooler blue-grey for Imerovigli, sun-bleached sand-gold for the beach coast) — perceptually distinct from every existing UK district accent and from each other. All four given kind 'city' (none fit the UK-specific 'county' distinction this field otherwise encodes) — they inherit the existing global dayMultiplier/bandMultiplier curves below rather than a bespoke holiday-town rhythm, an acknowledged imperfect fit (a beach town doesn't really have a Manchester office-worker's Mon-Fri pattern) not worth a per-metro schema change for a first pass. No district group added — with only four districts, the existing whole-metro 'Santorini' label (see metroWholeSetLabel below) already covers the zoomed-out labelling case a sub-group would otherwise handle.
_riyadhSource: Riyadh added 2026-09 at explicit user request — Curia's first fully separate real market, not a 'holiday' bolt-on like Santorini (see HomeRegion's own doc comment, src/types/models.ts, for the architecture this required: alcohol is prohibited nationwide, so Manchester/Cheshire's Drink catalog has zero applicability there, solved by a region-scoped onboarding Drink catalog rather than a product fork). Districts scaffolded first, deliberately with no venues yet (same starting point every new UK district — Chorlton, Didsbury, Stockport — has had before its own first curation pass), reviewed with the user before proceeding. Five real, distinct districts chosen to cover genuinely different Riyadh character rather than one undifferentiated blob: Olaya (the commercial/dining core along King Fahd Road — everyday cafes, shisha culture, international dining), King Abdullah Financial District/KAFD (a futuristic new financial district — contemporary restaurants and evening social spots for young professionals), Diriyah/Bujairi Terrace (the UNESCO-listed mud-brick old town, At-Turaif, now Riyadh's premier fine-dining terrace), JAX District (a former industrial site within Diriyah turned arts hub — SAMOCA, Saudi's first contemporary art museum, galleries, creative studios — deliberately kept as its own district from Bujairi Terrace despite both sitting within the broader Diriyah masterplan, since dining-heritage and arts-culture are genuinely different characters, the same 'split one place into real distinct areas' precedent Santorini's own four districts already set), and Hittin (the newest entertainment/lifestyle strip — Riyadh Boulevard/Boulevard City, Via Riyadh, U Walk — contemporary towers, often compared to Dubai). Coordinates verified via WebSearch against Wikipedia/Wikidata/Saudipedia rather than invented: Olaya 24.6957/46.6811 (Al Olaya district centroid, Wikipedia), KAFD 24.7628/46.6403 (Wikidata), Diriyah 24.7333/46.5756 (At-Turaif District, Wikipedia — matches the UNESCO listing's own coordinates), JAX District 24.7477/46.5329 (Saudipedia), Hittin 24.7503/46.6133 (Boulevard City, Wikipedia — the real, named anchor of Hittin's entertainment identity). accentColor values step outside the existing warm Manchester/Cheshire/Santorini palette into a distinct five-hue set, chosen for perceptual separation within the Riyadh cluster itself (the only districts that ever render together — per this file's own established precedent, a color only needs to be distinct from what's actually visible together, not from every metro globally): bronze-gold for Olaya's commercial bustle, steel-blue for KAFD's glass towers, clay-red for Diriyah's mud-brick heritage, deep plum for JAX's arts identity, and teal for Hittin's modern entertainment energy — the first teal used anywhere in this palette. All five given kind 'city' (matching Santorini's precedent — none fit the UK-specific 'county' distinction). base scores are reasoned estimates pending real curation, same convention as every other new district's first pass: Diriyah and Olaya sit highest (88/85 — genuinely constant, high-footfall destinations), Hittin next (82 — a newer but already-major evening strip), KAFD and JAX lower (65/60 — a business district that quiets on weekends, and a culture venue whose energy is more event-driven than nightly). Same acknowledged imperfect fit Santorini's own note already flags: the global dayMultiplier/bandMultiplier curves below assume a Mon-Fri UK working week, not Saudi Arabia's real Friday-Saturday weekend — not worth a per-metro schema change for a first pass, flagged rather than silently ignored. No district group added — five districts, same reasoning Santorini's own four gave: the whole-metro 'Riyadh' label (metroWholeSetLabel below) already covers the zoomed-out case.
_londonSource: London added 2026-09-15 at explicit user request — Curia's first UK-focused market outside Manchester/Cheshire, architecturally simpler than Santorini/Riyadh: London is fully 'uk' HomeRegion, so no onboarding Drink-catalog changes were needed (see HomeRegion's own doc comment, src/types/models.ts). Districts scaffolded first, deliberately with no venues yet, same starting point every new district gets before its own first curation pass — 6 candidates proposed and reviewed with the user before writing this, all 6 confirmed as-is. Six real, distinct districts chosen from London's actual affluent west/central core rather than one undifferentiated 'Chelsea-ish' blob: Knightsbridge (flagship luxury retail, Harrods), Chelsea (old family money, King's Road, long-term ownership over anything flashier), Mayfair (the most expensive address in the city — private members' clubs, hedge funds), Belgravia (Georgian stucco, embassies, the quietest of the six), Notting Hill (a more bohemian/creative flavour of wealth, Portobello Road), and St James's (palaces, gentlemen's clubs, Michelin density). Coordinates verified via WebSearch plus postcodes.io geocoding against each district's real, well-known anchor point rather than invented — the same postcode-geocoding methodology already used for Curia's venue coordinates: Knightsbridge 51.49945/-0.16321 (Harrods, SW1X 7XL), Chelsea 51.49261/-0.15640 (Sloane Square, SW1W 8AS), Mayfair 51.50988/-0.14456 (Berkeley Square, W1J 6BR), Belgravia 51.49817/-0.15426 (Belgrave Square, SW1X 8PZ), Notting Hill 51.50918/-0.19454 (Notting Hill Gate, W11 3JQ), St James's 51.50751/-0.13657 (St James's Square, SW1Y 4LB). accentColor values chosen for perceptual separation within the London cluster itself (the only districts that ever render together, per this file's own established precedent): amber-brass for Knightsbridge's retail energy, brick-terracotta for Chelsea, deep plum for Mayfair's clubland evenings, sage-stone for Belgravia's quiet Georgian elegance, teal-green for Notting Hill's colour and greenery, and slate-blue for St James's institutional formality. All six given kind 'city' — unlike Cheshire's county-town distinction, there's no meaningful 'county' vs 'city' split within inner London, so every district here reads as urban-dense the way Manchester's city districts do, and shares that global bandMultiplier curve rather than Cheshire's quieter county one. base scores are reasoned estimates pending real curation, same convention as every other new district's first pass: Mayfair highest (90 — genuinely the most consistently active address of the six), Knightsbridge next (86), Chelsea (80), Notting Hill (76), St James's (72), Belgravia lowest (60 — real, deliberate quiet: embassies and residential garden squares, not late-night venues). No district group added — six districts is still small enough that the whole-metro 'London' label (metroWholeSetLabel below) covers the zoomed-out case, same reasoning Santorini's four and Riyadh's five already established; worth revisiting if the set grows (Knightsbridge/Belgravia in particular share a real, named ward — 'Knightsbridge and Belgravia').
_hittinBoundaryCorrectionSource: 2026-09-15, at explicit discovery during the district's first venue-curation pass: the _riyadhSource note below describes Hittin as covering 'Riyadh Boulevard/Boulevard City, Via Riyadh, U Walk' — independent research for that pass found this overstates the real boundary. Boulevard City is solidly, consistently confirmed as being in Hittin (Prince Turki Al-Awwal Road, per Wikipedia, Arab News, Saudipedia and the General Entertainment Authority's own materials). Via Riyadh is not in Hittin — it's a separate luxury development in the Al-Hada district, on King Fahd Road. U Walk is also not consistently classified as Hittin — official/retail sources place it in Al Nakheel district (Prince Turki bin Abdulaziz Al Awwal Road), adjacent but distinct. This district's own editorialDescription/coordinates were never wrong (Boulevard City was always the real anchor, independently verified when Hittin was first scaffolded), only the older provenance note's supporting list of landmarks — left uncorrected there rather than rewritten, per this file's own practice of appending corrections instead of rewriting history (see _imerovigliCoordinateCorrectionSource for the same pattern). Practical effect: Hittin's real, verifiable independent venue base is thinner than the original note implied, since two of its three named anchors don't actually belong to this district — see docs/data/venues.json's own _riyadhVenueSource note for how this played out in that pass.

districts.name: Northern Quarter
districts.editorialDescription: Loudest of the ten, and honest about it. Best treated as a second or third stop rather than the whole evening — the good rooms are upstairs, behind doors with no signage.

districts.name: Ancoats
districts.editorialDescription: Mill brick and low ceilings, run by people who used to cook somewhere more famous and left on purpose. It peaks late and rewards walking — the best of it sits within a few minutes of the canal.

districts.name: Spinningfields
districts.editorialDescription: Glass, height and expense accounts. It empties by eleven on a weeknight, which is either the flaw or the appeal depending on the evening you had in mind.

districts.name: Deansgate
districts.editorialDescription: The formal spine of the city — hotel bars, height, and service that still wears a jacket. Reliable rather than surprising, which on a Tuesday is the point.

districts.name: Chinatown
districts.editorialDescription: Smaller than its name suggests, and better after dark than at lunch. A handful of rooms worth detouring for, tucked in behind the arch most people only photograph.

districts.name: Altrincham
districts.editorialDescription: A market town playing at being a city district, and mostly winning. Independent cinema, small plates, and a pizza queue nobody minds standing in.

districts.name: Hale
districts.editorialDescription: Village high street money — quieter than Altrincham, later than it looks from the outside. Best on a Friday, when the terrace tables fill before the sun goes.

districts.name: Wilmslow
districts.editorialDescription: The polished end of the Golden Triangle. Understated storefronts hiding rooms that assume you already know what you want.

districts.name: Alderley Edge
districts.editorialDescription: Sandstone and fireplaces, with the actual Edge — the wooded ridge, not a marketing name — a ten-minute walk from most of it. Earlier nights than the city, and no worse for it.

districts.name: Mobberley
districts.editorialDescription: The quiet edge of the set — fewer rooms, longer drives, and exactly the kind of evening that rewards both.

districts.name: Prestbury
districts.editorialDescription: The actual point of the Golden Triangle's compass — Tudor timber and a Norman chapel two centuries past the silk money that built most of it. Small enough that the whole village still counts as one recommendation.

districts.name: Cheadle Hulme
districts.editorialDescription: The quieter, greener edge of the set, closer to the city than any of Cheshire's other districts and unbothered by the comparison. A station platform into Manchester and a park worth the walk before dinner.

districts.name: Knutsford
districts.editorialDescription: A working market town before it's anything else — an indoor hall trading four days a week, a King Street that still closes for its own May Day procession, and Tatton Park's deer a mile up the road for whoever wants the grounds without the crowd.

districts.name: Chorlton
districts.editorialDescription: Three high streets and a green nobody rushes off of — Beech Road, Manchester Road and Wilbraham Road, each doing its own version of the same thing. More independent restaurants per acre than anywhere else in the city, a beer mile that means something, and the chain pub wave that swallowed everywhere else never quite got a foothold here.

districts.name: Didsbury
districts.editorialDescription: Victorian villas and two villages within one — Didsbury Village around School Lane, West Didsbury along Burton Road, half an hour from the city centre by tram and further than that in temperament. The kind of suburb where the fine-dining room and the Sunday jazz pub sit on the same postcode, and neither one apologises for the other.

districts.name: Stockport (Underbanks)
districts.editorialDescription: A Victorian market hall at one end and old bank vaults turned into wine bars at the other, with the steepest street in England running straight between them — the regeneration story every other northern town centre is quietly trying to copy.

districts.name: Heaton Moor
districts.editorialDescription: One of the Four Heatons, and the one with the actual high street — Heaton Moor Road and Shaw Road doing a quieter version of what Chorlton and Didsbury do further south. A 1923 cinema saved twice, most recently by a family who bought it back from the multiplex era, and a producers' market that still runs on a Saturday.

districts.name: Bramhall
districts.editorialDescription: A village green with a Tudor manor behind it and a shopping parade in front — the sort of Stockport postcode that would rather be mistaken for Cheshire, and mostly gets away with it.

districts.name: Macclesfield
districts.editorialDescription: The town that funded Prestbury's church and Alderley Edge's stone before either of them meant much — a royal charter in 1261, silk mills worked since into flats and museums both, and streets steep enough that the postcards apologise for them.

districts.name: Nantwich
districts.editorialDescription: A salt town before it was anything else — 'wich' means brine — with more black-and-white Tudor timber per street than the rest of the county put together, a medieval church at its centre, and a market that's run three days a week since long before most of Cheshire's other towns had a charter.

districts.name: Chester
districts.editorialDescription: Roman walls two thousand years old still ring the centre, and the Rows stack a second storey of shopfronts above the first — a working city that happens to be standing on its own ruins. The kind of place that earns its queue outside the better rooms, not just its postcard.

districts.name: Tarporley
districts.editorialDescription: The Cheshire village that resisted the chain-store drift entirely — butchers and a bookshop on the high street, a coaching inn that's poured drinks since 1565, and a farm shop a few minutes out that's fed the same family's customers since 1959.

districts.name: Northwich
districts.editorialDescription: Another salt town on the same river as Nantwich, rebuilding its own high street on its own terms — a rooftop bar over the water where the old quayside warehouses stood, and a bistro that's been quietly good since 2004.

districts.name: Oia
districts.editorialDescription: Blue domes and a nightly ritual — half the village turns out along the castle path to watch the sun drop into the caldera. Book a table an hour before it does, or don't bother.

districts.name: Fira
districts.editorialDescription: The island's actual town, not just its postcard — caldera-view terraces by day give way to the bars along the cliffside steps that stay loud till four.

districts.name: Imerovigli
districts.editorialDescription: The highest point on the rim, quieter than Oia for the same view, with the island's most serious hotel terraces and none of the crowds that come to watch the sunset elsewhere.

districts.name: Perissa & Perivolos
districts.editorialDescription: Black sand and a run of beach clubs that start serving before noon and don't stop — the island's actual daytime, once the caldera villages have gone quiet from the heat.

districts.name: Olaya
districts.editorialDescription: The city's real commercial spine, King Fahd Road running through the middle of it — cafes that don't close before one, and a shisha culture that's older than the towers around it.

districts.name: King Abdullah Financial District
districts.editorialDescription: Riyadh's newest skyline, built for the trading day and increasingly good after it ends — the evening crowd here is younger, and arrived by choice, not just by office.

districts.name: Diriyah
districts.editorialDescription: Mud-brick walls three centuries old and a terrace of dining rooms that opened in the last five years — At-Turaif's UNESCO listing sits a short walk from some of the country's most serious tables.

districts.name: JAX District
districts.editorialDescription: An industrial site turned gallery quarter — studios, a contemporary art museum, and the kind of exhibition openings that spill onto the street outside.

districts.name: Hittin
districts.editorialDescription: The new strip — towers, terraces, and a boulevard built for exactly this. The closest thing Riyadh has to a district that never quite finished being built, and is better for it.

districts.name: Knightsbridge
districts.editorialDescription: Harrods at one end, the museums at the other, and a density of five-figure handbags per square foot the rest of the country doesn't attempt. The restaurants behind the department stores are better than the ones inside them.

districts.name: Chelsea
districts.editorialDescription: Old money that never left, running the length of the King's Road from Sloane Square to World's End — long-term ownership over anything flashier, and unbothered by whoever's currently trying to buy their way in.

districts.name: Mayfair
districts.editorialDescription: Private members' clubs behind unmarked doors, hedge funds above the shopfronts, and dinner reservations made months out rather than days. The most expensive square on the board, and it still behaves like it.

districts.name: Belgravia
districts.editorialDescription: Stucco terraces and garden squares with their own keys — the quietest kind of wealth, more embassy than nightclub. Fewer rooms than its neighbours, and none of them need to try hard.

districts.name: Notting Hill
districts.editorialDescription: Pastel houses and a Saturday market that still pulls a crowd, but the real business happens on the quieter streets around it, at tables nobody's advertising.

districts.name: St James's
districts.editorialDescription: Gentlemen's clubs, one very famous hotel, and a concentration of Michelin stars that outweighs its size by a wide margin. Formal enough that most of it still expects a jacket.

districts.name: Hyde Park
districts.editorialDescription: A university town within a city, built around a Gothic quad and the stretch of 53rd and 57th that services it — secondhand bookshops that have outlasted their landlords twice over, a cafeteria line Obama used to queue in, and a Michelin Bib Gourmand two blocks from the lecture halls. Lake Michigan on one side, the Midway on the other, and just enough independent grit left in the storefronts that the neighbourhood still reads as lived-in, not curated.

districts.name: Kenwood
districts.editorialDescription: Chicago's grandest surviving mansion district, and still mostly houses — Muddy Waters kept one here, so did Louis Farrakhan, and the greystones on Greenwood and Woodlawn Avenue don't advertise who's inside. What commercial life there is runs thin and specific along 47th and 43rd: a Senegalese kitchen built on a family recipe from Dakar, a jazz room made out of a father's old TV-repair shop, nothing that needs a queue.

districts.name: Woodlawn
districts.editorialDescription: Ninety years of disinvestment couldn't quite finish Woodlawn off, and the Obama Presidential Center's arrival in Jackson Park hasn't rewritten it so much as given it a reason to be looked at again. What's here now is a real mix: a lunch counter that's fed the neighbourhood since 1892, a coffee shop a handful of regulars bought outright rather than watch it disappear, and a Saturday farmers market that was doing the work long before anyone called it a comeback.

_dayMultiplierSource: The prototype's DAY_MULT table is global (not per-district) — applied identically to every district by src/lib/data/seed.ts. Keys are full lowercase day names to match src/lib/scoring/rank-venues.ts's resolveContext() day format.
_bandMultiplierSource: The prototype's BAND_MULT table, keyed by District.kind ('city' vs 'county') — the default every district falls back to. A district can still carry its own per-district `bandMultiplier` override directly on its entry instead (District.bandMultiplier in src/types/models.ts, preferred over the kind-based table by src/lib/data/seed.ts whenever present) when sharing the generic curve would flatten real differences in character — used for Beverly Hills/West Hollywood during the LA metro's lifetime (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'make districts feel alive... different districts... busy at different times'), removed along with the rest of that metro (see _metroScopeNote). No district currently uses an override, but the mechanism stays — a genuine judgment call grounded in real character, not transcribed from the prototype (no per-district curve exists there), worth keeping for whatever district needs it next.
